cells.tense: You're standing at the finish right now, steady-handed, already easy about the end.
cells.ask: Say the ending out loud to one person while it's fresh — just 'that's done' — and stop there instead of tacking on the next thing; what you made gets to keep its size.
cells.core:
The last stretch is going well. You're tending it, both hands on, and there's no force in it. The thing is coming to its own end and you're letting that happen — nothing clutched, nothing dropped. It's quiet work, a little dull, and it's working.

When the end arrives, mark it where someone can hear you. Say plainly that it's finished, and then don't rush the next thing in to fill the space it leaves. What you carried sits in your hands and stays yours, and the time after it stays open.

cells.tense: You're standing past a finish that hasn't happened yet, steering hard toward it.
cells.ask: Pick one thing you keep adding to and leave it as it is for today — hands off — and notice what's already whole about it.
cells.core:
Done can be a plain thing here: the work reaches its end, you stop, and your hands go still while your attention moves on. The clutch is optional in that version, and it's still available to you.

What's happening instead is that you're living a few steps ahead, in the version where it lands right, so one more piece goes on and then one more. The pushing is what's tiring you. The thing stays just short of done and you stay just short of rest. Finished work doesn't announce itself, so leave one of them alone for a day and see how the care holds without the extra piece.

cells.tense: You're standing at a door that closed behind you, still holding what you didn't set down.
cells.ask: Find the thing you finished and didn't claim, and say out loud what it took out of you and what it left — one sentence, nothing added after it — and what comes next opens from there.
cells.core:
There is a finished version of this: something ends, you call it over, and you walk on with your hands free. It happens, and it's not dramatic when it does.

What's actually happening is that something you carried ended a while back and you stayed where it ended, still holding it, still not calling it finished. You still care, and that caring points at something already closed, so nothing new has a place to start. The wish to keep going stayed with you too, and that part is yours and it's what gets the next thing moving. Put one sentence on it: what you gave, what it gave back, said to someone. Then you can walk past where you've been standing.

cells.tense: The pen's on the table and something is still being carried in that room without you saying so.
cells.ask: Take one finished thing you've been calling luck or somebody else's doing, and say plainly what you put into it; saying it, once, is what lets the release land as yours.
cells.core:
A clean finish would sound like this: it's over, you know what you gave it, you say so out loud once, and then it's behind you. Nothing held back and nothing performed.

What you'd say instead is that circumstances lined up, or that it mostly took care of itself. You kept two demands going at once and the care shows in every part of it. What's missing is you saying so. Work nobody names, including the one who did it, starts to feel like a debt still owed — so name one piece of it in your own voice, once, and the ending stops feeling like something taken from you.
